newsitem.title: LEBANON: Kuwait, Lebanon, Egypt in market cross-listing deal. [CORRECTED 13:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, Lebanon, Egypt in market cross-listing deal. [CORRECTED 13:45 GMT]

text.p: The Lebanese, Egyptian and Kuwaiti stock exchanges signed a deal on Wednesday to begin cross-listing shares next year and officials said they hoped the Bahraini, Omani and Moroccan exchanges would soon join it.
Kuwaiti Stock Exchange Director-General Hisham al-Oteibi (corrects name and title from "President Hisham al-Utaibi") said the accord could lead to the creation of "one huge Arab stock exchange."

The heads of the three exchanges and the secretary-general of the Union of Arab Stock Exchanges, who signed the accord, will set up a committee to draft regulations for the three markets in accordance with international standards.
"The Arab investor will have an easier time investing, transferring and securing his investment under this legal umbrella," Oteibi said.

"Cross-listing will take place as soon as we create a unified clearing, settlement and custody institution and provide cross agreements between brokerage firms. That's exactly the job of the committee," he added.
Sa'faq al-Rukeibi, secretary-general of the Union of Arab Stock Exchanges, said he expected cross-listing to start in 1997.
Officials said the agreement would guarantee in its first stage a free flow of updated information to investors and dealers in the three markets.
It follows an initial accord in April between Egypt's Capital Markets Authority and the Kuwait Stock Exchange.

"We hope that the stock exchanges of Bahrain, Sultanate of Oman and Morocco will join us soon in this agreement. If we open up for all these stock exchanges we would be creating one huge Arab stock exchange," Oteibi said.
Lebanon's acting finance minister Fouad Siniora said the agreement would eventually activate Beirut's financial markets and attract Arab investment in the country.
"This will secure sources of financing for the private sector to allow it to play a big role in the economic development of Lebanon," Siniora said.
The market capitalisation of the Egyptian exchange is $10.5 billion and the Kuwait bourse's is $18 billion.

The Beirut Stock Exchange, which reopened in January after a shutdown of nearly 13 years, currently lists only four industrial companies with a capitalisation of less than $400 million. However, Lebanon's biggest company SOLIDERE, with a capitalisation of more than $2 billion, will be listed on the exchange starting on Monday.

Lebanese banks are expected to apply for listings soon under a recent law allowing them to trade 30 percent of their shares. The government must still approve technical details for implementing the law.
Oteibi said a bill opening Kuwaiti markets to foreign investors would be a priority on the agenda of the new Kuwaiti parliament to be elected on October 7.

"We have started taking steps towards allowing foreign investors to trade in Kuwaiti shares and the bill is in the corridors of the parliament. After the October 7 elections, it will be voted," he said.
